facts.detail: The postcode checker returns separate coverage and performance information for mobile networks.
Coverage is classified using indoor and outdoor categories including good, variable and poor-to-none outcomes.
Trees, buildings, hills, congestion, weather and handset characteristics can make real experience differ from predictions.
Where indoor calling is difficult, Ofcom suggests considering Wi-Fi calling over a broadband connection.

guard_streams.write_limit: Checker predictions and advice do not prove exact parcel coverage or measured performance.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Map Your Mobile and one-million-user update

facts.detail: Performance scores express the likelihood of successfully streaming video or making a video call where coverage exists.
Performance is summarised for the wider postal district and is not representative of national coverage.
Ofcom states performance scores should be treated as a guide because local variations remain.
The 29 May 2026 update reported one million users and described a mix of Opensignal crowdsourced experience and operator predictions.

guard_streams.write_limit: District-level and crowdsourced performance cannot be assigned to individual parcel rows.

facts.detail: Coverage maps use operator predictions generated by computer models of signal propagation and obstruction.
Predictions are processed into a 50 metre by 50 metre grid covering the UK landmass.
Ofcom validates predictions with real-world measurement samples, finding them generally reliable but not guaranteed locally.
Coverage is targeted for roughly quarterly updates, while the address dataset is refreshed three times a year.

guard_streams.write_limit: Model grids and sample validation remain predictions rather than exact parcel observations.

facts.detail: Using a separate Bluetooth earpiece rather than holding the phone to the ear may improve call reception.
Wi-Fi calling can help where mobile coverage is poor but a good Wi-Fi connection is available.
Not every handset supports Wi-Fi calling, so customers should check compatibility with the operator.
Ofcom notes consumers may have a 14-calendar-day cancellation right and should test coverage promptly.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reception tips and cancellation rights cannot establish network serviceability at a parcel.

facts.detail: Regulated providers must take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted access to emergency organisations for offered voice services.
Providers must make accurate and reliable caller-location information available for 999 and 112 calls where technically feasible.
The compliance programme opened on 31 October 2025 and closed on 8 June 2026.
The programme referenced General Conditions A3.2(b), A3.5 and A3.6.

guard_streams.write_limit: Emergency-call obligations are regulatory duties and do not prove parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The Northern Ireland Executive is the contracting authority for Project Gigabit contracts in Northern Ireland.
Fibrus is the awarded broadband provider.
The contract covers more than 9,000 premises across Northern Ireland.
The GOV.UK guidance was published on 16 December 2025 and directs users to the Northern Ireland Department for the Economy for details.

guard_streams.write_limit: National contract scope does not identify live service at a parcel.

facts.detail: Freedom Fibre is no longer delivering the Cheshire Project Gigabit contract.
BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually agreed to terminate the contract.
Freedom Fibre received no public funding under the terminated contract.
In February 2026, Openreach call-off eight was used for around 18,500 Cheshire premises with £37.5 million funding.

guard_streams.write_limit: Termination and replacement scope cannot establish which parcels are served.

guard_streams.source: BDUK West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract

facts.detail: BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract.
BDUK stated it was moving to put alternative supplier plans in place.
In April 2026, West Herefordshire premises were included within Openreach call-off three.
The reassignment update was published on 14 April 2026.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract reassignment is not exact parcel delivery evidence.

facts.detail: The original Kent contract covered around 50,000 premises for £112 million and was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced the contract to around 9,000 premises backed by £26.1 million.
The redesign followed significant commercial rollout expansion and changing market conditions.
Preparatory construction is required and premise lists remain subject to planning and technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesigned regional totals cannot be promoted to exact parcel availability.

facts.detail: The original Cambridgeshire contract covered up to 45,000 premises for £69 million and was signed in February 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 35,000 premises backed by up to £77 million.
The redesign focused public funding on premises not covered by expanded commercial rollout.
Trenching, duct and fibre work precede access, and premise scope can change for planning or technical reasons.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract redesign and planned construction do not prove current parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract

facts.detail: CityFibre is no longer delivering the Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract.
BDUK and CityFibre mutually agreed to end the contract.
The page attributes the decision to wider market conditions and significant commercial rollout expansion reducing the need for public funding.
BDUK states it is discussing alternatives for the few premises not covered by other rollout plans.

guard_streams.write_limit: A terminated contract and alternative discussions do not establish parcel service.

facts.detail: FullFibre is no longer delivering the Derbyshire Peak District contract.
BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the contract.
BDUK stated it was moving to put alternative plans in place.
In April 2026, the Peak District area was included in Openreach call-off one.

guard_streams.write_limit: Termination and call-off inclusion cannot identify completed parcel connections.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Dorset and South Somerset contract

facts.detail: Wessex Internet is the awarded supplier.
The contract value is £33.5 million.
The award targets around 21,400 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in March 2024 and requires planning and physical build before service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional award scope cannot establish exact current parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The July table records Openreach call-off eight for Cheshire at 18,460 contracted and zero built premises.
Cambridgeshire is recorded at 18,230 contracted and 12,030 built premises.
Dorset and South Somerset is recorded at 19,560 contracted and 5,030 built premises.
Kent is recorded at 8,750 contracted and 2,530 built premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded and lagged management snapshots cannot identify delivered parcels.

facts.detail: Canonical continuation and runtime records show no live owner.
No active or over-15-minute PENDING execution exists.
BDUK management data covers initial scope, is rounded and lagged, and is not directly comparable with official statistics.
No candidate, measured-speed row or accuracy promotion is allowed before accepted r2 bytes, exact join and hardened postjoin readback.

guard_streams.write_limit: Final completion still requires canonical Windows-host archive and postjoin evidence.
